title: Box Her Before You Roll
hook: Gracie is on the dash. Box her before you roll.
scene: You unclip the carrier in a Kent work zone at dusk, overcast, cones leaning like they are tired. Gracie hits the dash like she owns the defrost. Orange tabby, cream chest, amber-green eyes, already in the way of the right side mirror. This is the passenger problem with a face. She will stand up at the wrong bus. She will walk a keyboard you do not have. The Grid still has eight cards of space and night and ice in it. If she is loose, she is a lap. If she is boxed, she is a sound you can ignore. You have to choose before the next roll, not during it.
decision: Gracie is on the dash. What do you do before you roll?

options.text: Clip her back in the carrier and stow it before you roll
options.result: You box her. The clip bites. She complains once and then she is a sound on the floor next to the seat, not a face on the glass. Your eyes stay on the torn-up road, not on a cream chest that wants the defrost.

options.text: Leave her. She will settle once the Menace starts rolling
options.result: She does not settle. She stands into the right side mirror as you enter the work zone. Your eyes go to her. The cone line does not wait. A cone kisses the plow with a note you will hear next to the seat for a block.

options.text: Pull her into your lap so she is off the glass
options.result: Mass in your legs. She kneads. Your right foot is a negotiation. A work zone does not care that you have a cat. You wander an inch and the cone line teaches you the width of a lap.

options.text: Let her walk the dash. You can watch her and the cones at once
options.result: You cannot. She takes the defrost. Your eyes leave the cones. The next cone is closer than the last one looked. Two jobs, one pair of eyes, and the work zone does not pause for cream fur.

debrief: Unrestrained passengers — including a cat — are a distraction with mass. Eyes that go to the dash leave the cones. Clip her in, then roll.

source.teaching_target: Restrain passengers and pets; a moving animal in the cab is a distraction event, not flavor.

image_brief.subject: Gracie the orange tabby sitting in the defrost, cream chest, amber-green eyes, one paw on the top of the cracked pink dash
image_brief.foreground: the carrier door hanging open, a clip undone
image_brief.midground: Ali's wire rims and cranberry braid out of focus behind the cat, not looking at the road
image_brief.background: work-zone cones through the mesh at dusk, overcast, no sun
image_brief.read: the cat is on the dash and the driver's eyes are on the cat
